description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Astera Neuro seeks to understand and engineer consciousness. We believe consciousness is the process by which the brain builds a coherent internal model of the world and the self. We aim to understand this model and to develop the technologies to write experience directly into the brain. By combining large-scale neural recording, causal perturbation, and brain-based AI, we seek to move neuroscience from observing correlates of experience to engineering it. The same tools carry direct therapeutic promise for neurological and psychiatric diseases that alter perception, thought, and sense of self. Because the science and tools required do not yet exist, we are assembling a founding team of neuroscientists, theorists, and engineers to create them. We do high-risk, high-reward science in a well-resourced, collaborative environment with competitive pay, and share everything openly under Astera's Open Science Policy.


POSITION SUMMARY

Research Scientists in NeuroAI at Astera Neuro develop and lead research programs aimed at understanding how the brain builds a model of the physical world, forms new thoughts, and creates a stable model of the self. The goal is enough understanding and technical ability to precisely and reversibly modulate each of these functions through write-in experiments.

You will bring modern AI and machine learning methods to large-scale neural and behavioral recordings from our primate, rodent, and human programs. Working closely with experimental neuroscientists and engineers, you will build models that uncover how neural circuits in artificial and biological networks represent information and compute, and use those models to guide closed-loop experiments and targeted neural perturbations. This role suits researchers whose primary training is in machine learning; prior neuroscience experience is welcome but not required. Title and scope are calibrated to track record.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Develop and lead a machine learning research program to understand how the brain builds an internal model of the world, composes structured thoughts, and guides flexible behavior.

 - Train foundation models that align neural activity with sensory inputs and behavior across recording sessions, subjects, and species, enabling in silico experiments and closed-loop control of neural activity.

 - Develop mechanistic interpretability and representation analysis methods to uncover how artificial and biological networks compute, and analyze how neural geometry evolves over time and across task contexts.

 - Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists to test model predictions in vivo, designing behavioral tasks and closed-loop write-in perturbations that steer neural activity to alter percepts, thoughts, or internal states.

 - Translate computational principles discovered in the brain into new AI architectures and learning algorithms.

 - Mentor research engineers and, at the senior or principal level, more junior scientists; contribute to hiring, onboarding, and lab culture.

 - Contribute to publications, talks, open data and tooling releases, and engagement with the broader scientific community.


WHO YOU ARE

Required:

 - PhD with 3-12+ years of experience in machine learning, computer science, computational neuroscience, physics, applied mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent research experience.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead original machine learning research end to end, with depth in areas such as mechanistic interpretability, representation learning, reinforcement learning, world models, or foundation models.

 - Strong programming and research engineering skills in Python and PyTorch or JAX, with experience building custom architectures, learning objectives, or interpretability tools at scale.

 - Ability to collaborate closely with neuroscientists and engineers in a fast-moving, interdisciplinary environment.

Preferred/Nice to Have:

 - Experience in neuroscience, especially collaborating closely with experimentalists, analyzing large-scale neural and behavioral recordings, or conducting experimental work.

 - Experience connecting the internal computations of artificial networks to biological circuits, or designing model-guided, closed-loop neural perturbation experiments.

 - Experience scaling training and data pipelines across large, heterogeneous datasets, and contributing to ML or scientific tooling.


WHAT WE VALUE

 - Deep interest in understanding intelligence in biological and artificial systems.

 - Conviction that the brain’s internal model can be understood in full, and recognition that getting there requires a kind of science no single academic lab can do.

 - Willingness to be held to an engineering standard: our decisive tests are write-in experiments, not merely decoding. What we cannot build, we do not understand.

 - Comfort building on shared infrastructure rather than private projects.

 - Commitment to open science, including releasing code, models, and data publicly.


ADDITIONALLY EXPECTED AT SENIOR / PRINCIPAL LEVEL

 - Experience setting research direction and leading collaborative projects across disciplines.

 - Track record of mentorship and technical leadership.


WHY JOIN US

Join Astera Neuro to work on the hardest and least understood questions in neuroscience: how the brain generates thoughts, intelligence, and consciousness. You will bring machine learning into close contact with large-scale neural experiments, building models that explain biological computation and using discoveries about the brain to inform new approaches to AI.

Astera Neuro provides a comprehensive benefits package and total compensation that is competitive and commensurate with the level of experience and qualifications.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity and inclusion!
